The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

" Get the intersection of the instance and another sub-line. *

* This method is related to the {@link Line#intersection(Line) * intersection} method in the {@link Line Line} class, but in addition * to compute the point along infinite lines, it also checks the point * lies on both sub-line ranges. *

* @param subLine other sub-line which may intersect instance * @param includeEndPoints if true, endpoints are considered to belong to * instance (i.e. they are closed sets) and may be returned, otherwise endpoints * are considered to not belong to instance (i.e. they are open sets) and intersection * occurring on endpoints lead to null being returned * @return the intersection point if there is one, null if the sub-lines don't intersect "

Title: Diagnosis

Details: The test `testIntersectionParallel()` creates two parallel SubLine objects that do not intersect. When calling `sub1.intersection(sub2, true)`, a NullPointerException is thrown. The root cause analysis is as follows:

1. In `SubLine.intersection(SubLine, boolean)`, the two underlying Lines are retrieved via `getHyperplane()`.
2. The `Line.intersection(Line)` method is then called to get the intersection point of these infinite lines.
3. If the lines are parallel (or coincident), `Line.intersection()` returns `null` (lines 199-201).
4. Immediately after, `SubLine.intersection()` calls `line1.toSubSpace(v2D)` where `v2D` is the intersection point just obtained.
5. Since `v2D` is `null` for parallel lines, `line1.toSubSpace` throws a NullPointerException because it tries to use the coordinates of a null Vector2D.
6. The `SubLine.intersection` method lacks a null check on the intersection result before passing it into `toSubSpace()`.
7. This causes the NPE when two SubLines that do not intersect are tested.

Therefore, the bug occurs due to missing defensive null checking after computing the intersection point in `SubLine.intersection`. It expects a non-null intersection vector, but parallel lines return null, causing the subsequent call to fail.

The correct fix would be to check if the result of `line1.intersection(line2)` is null before invoking `toSubSpace` on it and return null early if so. This would prevent the NullPointerException and properly indicate no intersection.

This diagnosis matches the bug report which states an NPE happens in `Line.toSubSpace()` when intersecting non-intersecting SubLines, specifically parallel lines.

The failing test verifies this scenario by intersecting two vertical lines at x=0 and x=66 with no overlap, expecting a null result but instead triggering an NPE.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
